model.name: Education / Qualification
model.purpose: Represent a person's source-qualified learning path, assessed outcomes, qualification awards, credentials and recognition decisions independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns learner-programme bindings, progress, outcome and result references, personal awards, credential lifecycle links, transcripts, comparability and recognition assertions, disclosure and provenance. External systems own people, institutions, programmes, courses, teaching, assessments, skills, occupations, licences, payments, immigration, consent and cryptographic proof infrastructure.
in_scope: Education systems, programme and qualification references, learner admission, enrolment, pathway, credit and prior learning
Learning outcomes, assessment evidence, grades, validation, qualification award, conferral and credential lifecycle
Transcripts, portability, comparability, recognition, disclosure, provenance, standards mappings and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Person and institution identity, teaching content and delivery, assessment execution, skills and occupation taxonomy masters
Professional licensure, immigration or admission decisions, payment, funding and cryptographic implementation
Universal grade, credit, framework, recognition, privacy, retention or minor-learner rules

boundary_notes.distinction: Reusable offerings and teaching execution keep their own masters; this model stores learner bindings, requirements and result links.
Assessment owns instruments, attempts and evaluation execution; the learner record stores evidence references, original result and competent validation effect.
The qualification is reusable, the award is a competent person-specific decision, and the credential is issuer-controlled evidence with an independent status lifecycle.
External taxonomies own concept meaning; education assertions store versioned alignments and demonstrated levels without remastering them.
A qualification can be evidence for a downstream licence or admission decision but never grants that authorization automatically.
Subject identity, access decisions and cryptographic execution remain external; this model records bindings, purpose and evidence.

sources.relevance: Defines the eight-level EQF reference framework based on learning outcomes and principles for comparing national qualification levels without automatic equivalence.

sources.title: European Qualifications Framework
sources.version_or_date: Current public framework service, accessed 6 September 2026
sources.relevance: Publishes national framework comparisons, learning-outcome level descriptors and qualification registers used for attributable comparability references.

sources.title: ESCO Qualifications
sources.relevance: Defines qualification records supplied by competent national sources and distinguishes qualification information from ESCO skills and occupations.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: Provides issuer, credential subject, claims, validity, status, schema, evidence, terms of use and presentations for portable education credentials.

sources.title: Comprehensive Learner Record Standard
sources.relevance: Provides a learner-controlled record for achievements, competencies, courses, skills and evidence and aligns with Open Badges and verifiable credentials.

sources.title: Open Badges
sources.version_or_date: Open Badges 3.0 public standard, accessed 6 September 2026
sources.relevance: Provides issuer, achievement, criteria, evidence, recipient, validity and status semantics for portable achievement credentials.

sources.title: Credential Transparency Description Language Handbook
sources.version_or_date: Current CTDL schema handbook, accessed 6 September 2026
sources.relevance: Provides structured descriptions of credentials, organizations, assessments, learning opportunities, conditions, costs, outcomes and quality-assurance relationships.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Provides attribution, association, delegation, derivation, revision and provenance bundles for programme, assessment, award, credential and recognition assertions.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines timestamps with seconds and explicit UTC relation for enrolment, assessment, conferral, issuance, recognition, verification and revocation events.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension identity, owner, learner-record steward, registrar, awarding authority and namespace
Person, institution, programme, course, activity, assessment, competency, occupation, credential, consent, evidence and decision registries
Master-system mappings for learner, programme, enrolment, result, award, credential, recognition and lifecycle-event identifiers
Classification, credit, grading, award, recognition, privacy, sealed-record, retention, federation and autonomous-agent policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint learner-record, award and assertion identifiers in the adopting Dimension only when no authoritative registrar or awarding-body identifier exists; preserve people, institutions, programmes, components, assessments, skills, occupations, licences, credentials, consents and evidence as typed references.
registry_links: Dimension-local programme, enrolment, outcome, award, credential, recognition and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize programmes, qualifications, learner records, awards and credentials by their own authoritative master-system identifiers and issuers, never by title, learner name, grade, date or hash alone.
Keep participation, attendance, completion, achievement, qualification definition, personal award, credential, recognition and professional authorization lifecycles distinct.
patch_rules: Additive extensions declare target bundle, layer or finding, education and jurisdiction profile, source, authority, privacy and interoperability impact.

Identity, rule, framework, scale, credit, award, subject-binding, status or recognition-semantic changes require a successor version, migration map, rollback and continued resolution of prior records.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when learner binding, authority, rules, framework, scale, evidence, award, credential status, privacy and provenance remain intact.
ISCED, EQF, national framework, ESCO, CTDL, CLR, Open Badges and VC mappings pin source and target versions and disclose transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for the programme, award, credential or recognition record, qualified by issuer.
Governed globally resolvable IRI with explicit registrar or awarding-body binding.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record events in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit UTC offset or Z; keep learning, assessment, decision, conferral, issue, revocation, verification and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {learner-record-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use learner name, title, grade, date, filename or hash alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and profile versions, authority, event and knowledge times, provenance, assurance, licence and access marking for every retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may register programmes, enrol learners, validate results, confer awards, issue credentials, recognize qualifications, disclose records, correct and revoke.
Participation, completion, achievement, qualification, award, credential, recognition and professional authorization are non-equivalent and cannot be inferred from each other without evidence.
Original grades, credits, scales, framework levels and terminology are preserved before any mapped value, and mappings never imply automatic equivalence.
Learners receive lawful access, portability, correction and disclosure control while registrars and awarding bodies retain source custody and statutory duties.
Automated agents may validate, map and assemble within policy; award, adverse correction, revocation, recognition and wider disclosure require accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, learner and role, purpose, source masters, valid and knowledge time, credential status and access scope; return minimum necessary education claims.
create: Create stable identities, learner and authority references, source provenance, framework and rule versions and explicit unknowns before participation, outcome or award claims.
update: Append assertion, decision, mapping or successor with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 time, evidence and validation; never overwrite a cited result, award or credential.
delete: Apply learner rights, registrar duties, sealed-record, appeal, legal-hold, credential-status and retention policy; prefer restriction or tombstone and never cascade to external masters.

roles.name: Privacy and records steward

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and disclosure of learner identity, participation, grades, incomplete work, sealed records, awards and credentials unless active Dimension, role, purpose and field policy grant it; expose the minimum claim.
exceptions: Statutory, judicial, safeguarding or emergency access must cite authority, be purpose-bound, attributable and reviewable and must not erase original results, appeals or audit evidence.
audit_requirements: Log actor, calling agent, role, purpose, learner, programme, award and credential identities, action, policy, RFC 3339 timestamp, effective authority, disclosed fields, evidence and outcome.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension-owner AGENTS.md, learner identity, registrar, award, recognition, privacy, sealed-record, retention and federation policies.

Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required person, institution, programme, assessment, competency, occupation, credential, consent and evidence instructions before mutation or disclosure.

coverage.claim: Covers a learner-centred education and qualification context from frameworks and enrolment through outcomes, awards, credentials, recognition, privacy and exchange.

checklist.notes: Programme, enrolment, qualification, award, credential, transcript and recognition identities and issuers are explicit.
ISCED, qualification-framework, award and credential classes are versioned and non-equivalent.
Programme rules, enrolment, outcomes, results, grades, credits, award claims and credential status are first-class.
Assessment, issuer, proof, status and recognition methods, evidence, time and confidence are covered.
Register, enrol, complete, assess, award, issue, correct, recognize, verify and project operations are governed.
People, institutions, content, activities, assessments, skills, occupations, licences, consent and proof systems stay external.
Admission, enrolment, progress, result, award, issue, correction, reissue, suspension, revocation and tombstone preserve history.
Learner, provider, registrar, assessor, awarding body, issuer, verifier and recognizing authority are typed and time-qualified.
Learning, assessment, decision, conferral, issue, revocation, verification and ingestion times remain distinct.
Jurisdiction, delivery location and recognition territory are referenced when material and privacy-controlled.
Sources, assessors, decisions, derivations, revisions, mappings and presentations remain attributable.
Learner interests, registrar custody, awarding authority, issuer status and recognizing authority remain separate.
Identity, authority, rules, scales, credit, evidence, status, mapping loss and stale verification are checked.
Minimum disclosure, sealed records, subject binding, consent, verifier purpose and audit are covered.
Appeals, statutory retention, holds, correction, revocation status and tombstones are explicit.
ISCED, EQF, national frameworks, ESCO, CTDL, CLR, Open Badges and VC mappings are versioned and loss-aware.

known_omissions: No independent Claude or Grok result was available; later external and education-sector review is required before canonical promotion.
National programme, credit, grade, framework, award, recognition, minor-learner, sealed-record, retention and appeal profiles require specialist review.
Teaching content and events, assessment execution, skills and occupation taxonomies, professional licences, payments, immigration and proof infrastructure remain external.
The frozen relation ledger contains no approved WM-PER-008 rows; composition targets remain draft.
Certified ISCED, EQF, ESCO, CTDL, CLR, Open Badges and VC crosswalks, conformance tests and licence review remain future work.
conflicts: Framework levels support comparability but do not prove qualification equivalence or recognition for a particular purpose.
A credential can be revoked, reissued or unavailable while the underlying learning or award remains historically true, and an award can be corrected without erasing completed learning.
Registrar, awarding body, credential issuer and recognizing authority may be different parties with conflicting assertions.
regional_assumptions: The EQF and ESCO supply European profiles and do not create universal levels, recognition or rights.
ISCED is a statistical classification and does not itself accredit a programme or confer a qualification.
CLR, Open Badges and Verifiable Credentials are exchange formats and do not determine educational quality, award authority or legal recognition.
adversarial_checks: Reject attendance or course completion represented as assessed achievement, qualification, award or professional authorization without explicit evidence.
Reject a qualification identity derived only from title, provider name, learner, grade or date.
Reject mapped credits, grades or levels that omit original system, scale, version, authority and non-equivalence caveat.
Reject public verification that leaks full transcript, sealed records, unnecessary identifiers or unrelated achievements.
Reject agent conferral, recognition, revocation, adverse correction or disclosure beyond current role, authority, purpose and confirmation class.
